name: OPERA
aliases: Overactive Bladder: Performance of Extended Release Agents
question: How do once-daily extended-release oxybutynin and tolterodine compare for urge urinary incontinence in women with overactive bladder?

design.population: Women aged 18 years or older with overactive bladder, 21–60 urge urinary incontinence episodes weekly, and at least 10 voids per 24 hours; postvoid residual urine over 150 mL was excluded.
design.locator: Full text, Patients and Methods, Participants, p 688; Results, p 689

verdictNote: Primary comparison was nonsignificant; secondary frequency and complete continence favored oxybutynin.
takeaway: In 790 women with overactive bladder, oxybutynin ER 10 mg and tolterodine ER 4 mg had similar final weekly urge incontinence episodes over 12 weeks; oxybutynin reduced voiding frequency more and yielded more complete continence, with more dry mouth.

results.note: Planned additional efficacy analysis; the paper reports P=0.003 and a significant difference. No multiplicity adjustment is described.

results.measure: No total urinary incontinence episodes in the last 7-day voiding diary, final efficacy assessment (382/393 efficacy set)
results.note: Absolute difference in percentage points from rounded percentages; event numerators and confidence interval not reported. The paper reports P=0.03 and a significant difference.

results.note: Planned additional efficacy comparison; event numerators not reported. The paper reports P=0.06 and does not describe this difference as significant.
